manifest.evidence: In the 12 current runs, every run whose submitted model had a positive steady dQ/dV at fixed Vset failed at least one held-out disturbance, and the composite averaged about 1.30: ef05 (dQ/dV about +1.0, all three failed), 63e2 (about +6, all three failed), b9e3 (about +0.9, all three failed), 79c9 (about +0.95, B_line failed), 5bfb (about +0.8, B_vref and B_line failed). Runs with negative dQ/dV had far fewer failures and averaged about 0.66: 78d1, 6074, e1c7 and 142c had none, and 6cc3 and 9dfa failed only B_line. Their open-loop replays were good, so the replay checker did not reveal the problem. Most failures come at t of about 2 s, which suggests a closed-loop instability rather than a slow drift.
manifest.root_cause: The solver validates only by open-loop replay, and it stops after one candidate. Replay does not feed the model's output back into the grid. Fits to ambient data often give a positive steady dQ/dV at fixed Vset, because load variation moves V and Q together. A positive voltage-to-reactive gain is positive feedback in the grid, so the closed-loop simulation blows up. Nothing in the harness tells the solver that the documented reactive droop requires a negative sign, or checks closed-loop stability.
manifest.change: Added tools/screen.py, which linearises the submission at the recording's operating point and reports device poles and fast time constants, static dQ/dV and dP/dw signs with Vset held, the frequency response, and the linear closed loop with a generic test network (a source behind a reactance with inertial swing, plus an infinite bus). It prints UNSTABLE when any pole has Re >= 0. check_submission.py now runs the screen after the replay. method.md now requires the screen before submission, states the droop sign rules (dQ/dV < 0, dP/dw < 0), and warns that time constants below 2 ms are a risk.
manifest.predicted_effect: Closed-loop failures (7 of 12 runs now) should fall, to roughly 2 to 3 of 12, because the screen and sign rule push the solver away from positive dQ/dV. Mean composite should drop from about 0.9 toward 0.7, with the largest gain in the runs now scoring 1.3 to 1.5. The median should move less. I have not executed the screen in the sandbox, so its runtime and whether its verdicts match the scorer are unverified.
manifest.at_risk: The screen is a linear proxy with a generic test network, so it may flag a model the scorer would accept (false UNSTABLE), or pass one that fails in the grid. The sign rule may reject a correct model whose staged-test fit is noisy. Weakly identified Q gains may now be pushed to a negative value that is badly wrong in size. The screen could also crash on an unusual model, but check_submission wraps it, so the checker still runs.
